einzeiler: David Wallace-Wells on AI politics, immigration data, and climate realities.
kurzfassung: Tim Miller is joined by David Wallace-Wells to discuss the shifting political landscape around AI data centers and tech oligarchs. They also examine the ongoing surge in ICE deportations and the compounding pressures of global climate change and El Niño. The conversation highlights widespread public distrust in tech leaders and the complex challenges of planetary adaptation.
stichpunkte: Three-quarters of Americans oppose local data center construction, fueling a novel populist backlash against tech oligarchs.
Politicians across the political spectrum, including Josh Shapiro and Greg Abbott, are aligning with data center opposition.
Widespread public distrust in tech leaders stems from a deep-seated feeling of powerlessness and economic alienation.
ICE arrests and deportations are hitting new highs, increasingly targeting law-abiding immigrants who comply with legal processes.
ICE has become the best-funded federal law enforcement agency, outpacing several military branches with a $75 billion budget.
Climate impacts are intensifying, with scientists noting increased climate sensitivity and severe heat waves globally.
An unprecedented El Niño event threatens global food production and could drive up food prices significantly.
beschreibung:
Mark the summer of 2026 as the moment when an unlikely supermajority of Americans came together on one issue: their opposition to data centers. This new, big, messy coalition spans the political spectrum and is rooted in a fear that the sociopaths of Silicon Valley will determine the future of our lives, our communities, and our economic prospects. And (most) politicians have noticed which way the wind is blowing. Plus: Carbon emissions are getting better but the planet is still getting warmer, the coming El Niño may be the strongest ever, and ICE arrests are dramatically up because Stephen Miller is siccing agents on immigrants who are following the rules.
The New York Times' David Wallace-Wells joins Tim Miller.
